item.stem:
The diagram shows transversal $t$ crossing lines $p$ and $q$. Angle $1$ sits above $p$ and to the right of $t$. Angle $2$ sits above $q$ and to the right of $t$.

Which claim about angles $1$ and $2$ is correct?

options.A: Angles $1$ and $2$ are corresponding angles, because each sits in the same matching position at its crossing.
options.B: Angles $1$ and $2$ are corresponding angles even when both are taken from the crossing with $p$ alone.
options.C: Angles $1$ and $2$ are same-side interior angles, so their measures must sum to $180^{\circ}$.
options.D: Angles $1$ and $2$ are corresponding angles only because the printed labels are $1$ and $2$.
